analysis.overall: You spent 87% of the day in range, but aggressive correction boluses following meal- and low-treatment carbs created a sharp late-morning roller coaster.

events.title: Afternoon spike
events.description: Glucose drifted up to a peak of 204 mg/dL. Micro-corrections gradually pulled it back into target range over the next hour.

events.title: Overnight correction drop
events.description: A late-night rise to 169 mg/dL prompted several small corrections, dropping you down to 80 mg/dL by 3:20 AM where you stayed steady through the night.

events.title: Extended morning low
events.description: Glucose drifted down into the mid-60s during the morning, staying low for nearly an hour before breakfast.

events.title: Post-breakfast spike
events.description: After eating 30g of carbs to recover from the low, glucose shot up quickly to peak at 215 mg/dL.

events.title: Early afternoon low
events.description: Multiple correction boluses on top of your meal insulin drove a sharp drop down to 59 mg/dL, requiring 36g of carbs to treat.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Watch out for stacking correction boluses shortly after treating a low, as the combined insulin can cause a rapid downward crash.
